mainTopic: Which merit delays a סוטה's punishment, and the power of Torah compared with a מצוה
overview: The גמרא finishes matching the משנה's rule, that merit can hold off a סוטה's punishment for up to three years, to רבי ישמעאל. His twelve-month delay can repeat up to three times, and he calls his source only a hint because non-Jews may be judged differently. The גמרא then asks which merit does the delaying. Torah study seems ruled out because a woman is not commanded to learn. The merit of a מצוה is also questioned, since a ברייתא compares a מצוה to a lamp that protects only for a while, and Torah to sunlight that protects forever. The ברייתא also adds a parable about a man walking in the dark. רב יוסף and then רבא explain that a מצוה still protects from suffering after it is done. רבינא says instead that a woman shares the Torah merit of her sons and husband. The amud ends by explaining the parable's crossroads, the mistake of דואג and אחיתופל, and the story of הלל and שבנא, which shows that money cannot buy a share in Torah after the learning is done.

steps.title: End of רבי ישמעאל's proof from נבוכדנצר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the פסוקים רבי ישמעאל used to show that merit can delay punishment for twelve months. This closes the challenge that no opinion in the ברייתא matches the משנה's 'three years'.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...and then there shall be an extension to your tranquility.' And it is written: 'All this came upon King נבוכדנצר.' And it is written: 'At the end of twelve months.' So none of the opinions fit the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of רבי ישמעאל's proof that merit delays punishment for twelve months. Since he says one year and the משנה says three years, it seems no opinion matches the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דניאל told נבוכדנצר that giving charity could delay his punishment. The punishment came only twelve months later, so merit delays punishment for one year. That leaves the משנה's 'three years' without a source, which is the problem the גמרא now has to solve.

keyTerms.meaning: King of בבל, the king in ספר דניאל

phrases.english: and then there shall be an extension to your tranquility.
phrases.notes: דניאל 4:24. We're joining the end of a פסוק רבי ישמעאל was quoting: give charity and your good times may last longer.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'All this came upon King Nebuchadnezzar,'
phrases.notes: דניאל 4:25

phrases.english: and it is written: 'At the end of twelve months'!
phrases.notes: דניאל 4:26. The punishment came only after twelve months, so merit held it off for one year, not three. That's the challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the ברייתא from before this section, which the גמרא is using to ask whose view the משנה follows.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ישמעאל's view that merit delays punishment for twelve months
steps.raayaSupportSource: דניאל 4:24 to 4:26, the story of נבוכדנצר's delayed punishment
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the משנה's 'three years' matches some opinion in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל proves from נבוכדנצר that merit delays punishment only twelve months, so he cannot be the source of the משנה's three years.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל: the delay can repeat three times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה does follow רבי ישמעאל. A פסוק about אדום shows the one-year delay can happen again and again, up to three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל. He found a פסוק that says it and says it again, as it is written: 'Thus says ה׳: For three transgressions of אדום...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by saying the משנה really is רבי ישמעאל. It brings a פסוק showing that a delay can be repeated up to three times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל taught that one round of delay lasts a year. The פסוק in עמוס says ה׳ held back punishment for three sins but not for a fourth, which shows a delay can be repeated up to three times. One year times three gives the משנה's three years.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually: keeps the original idea and explains it
That says it and repeats it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the משנה's 'one year, two years, three years' as one idea: the same one-year delay, repeated up to three times.

phrases.english: Actually, it is Rabbi Yishmael,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל after all.

phrases.english: and he found a verse which states and repeats,
as it is written: 'Thus says the Lord:
For three transgressions of Edom.'
phrases.notes: עמוס 1:11. The rest of the פסוק says 'but for four I will not take it back': three delays, then punishment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that no opinion in the ברייתא fits the משנה's three years.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets: the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, plus a second פסוק showing the delay repeats.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל allows only a single twelve-month delay, so he cannot match three years.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל's one-year delay can repeat up to three times, which matches the משנה.

steps.title: Why did רבי ישמעאל call it only a hint?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל said there is 'no proof, only a hint' when the פסוקים seem to say the twelve-month delay openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does רבי ישמעאל mean by saying 'although there is no proof for the matter, there is a hint for the matter'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about רבי ישמעאל's wording. The פסוקים about נבוכדנצר clearly show a twelve-month delay, so why call it only a hint?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'זכר' is a weaker support than a 'ראיה'. Here the story spells out a twelve-month delay. So the גמרא wants to know what keeps this from counting as a real proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A hint or reminder of the idea, weaker than a proof

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה
phrases.english: And what is meant by 'although there is no proof
for the matter, there is a hint for the matter'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the wording of רבי ישמעאל's statement in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי ישמעאל's source counts only as a hint and not a full proof.

steps.title: Non-Jews may be judged differently
steps.stepSummary: The answer: נבוכדנצר was not Jewish, and maybe non-Jews are not judged as quickly. So his story may not prove how long a Jew's merit delays punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps non-Jews are different, since judgment is not carried out on them so closely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'only a hint' wording. Maybe non-Jews are given more time, so a king's story cannot fully prove the rule for a Jewish סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ judges the Jewish people more strictly and more quickly. A long delay for a non-Jewish king might come from that looser judging, not from his merit. So the story only hints at the rule and does not prove it.

keyTerms.meaning: Judgment is carried out, judged closely

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל's twelve months comes from a non-Jewish king, so it counts only as a 'זכר'. Non-Jews may simply not be judged as quickly.

phrases.english: Perhaps gentiles are different,
since judgment is not closely administered upon them.
phrases.notes: He means ה׳ doesn't watch them as strictly, so a delay for them may have nothing to do with merit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about why the source is called only a hint.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source involves a non-Jew, and non-Jews may be judged less strictly, so it cannot fully prove the rule for Jews.

steps.title: Which merit delays the punishment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, 'there is a merit that delays for three years', and asks which merit it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And there is a merit that delays three years.' Merit of what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and starts a new topic. It asks what kind of merit could hold off a סוטה's punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was how long the delay lasts. Now the question is what causes it. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא tries out possible answers.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ זְכוּת תּוֹלָה שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: 'And there is a merit that delays three years,' etc.
Merit of what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of how long and returns to the משנה to ask what kind of merit is meant.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of merit protects a סוטה from immediate punishment.

steps.title: Torah study can't be it: she isn't commanded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the merit of Torah study and rejects it right away. A woman is not commanded to learn Torah, and doing a good deed without being commanded earns less.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is the merit of Torah, but she is one who is not commanded and does it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one answer, the merit of Torah, and knocks it down in the same breath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that someone commanded to do a מצוה gets more reward than someone who does it voluntarily. A woman is not obligated in Torah study, so her learning brings smaller merit, too weak to delay her punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Not commanded but does it anyway (less reward)

steps.confusionAlert: This doesn't mean a woman's Torah learning is worthless. It means its merit is smaller than that of someone obligated, too small for this purpose.

phrases.english: If we say it is the merit of Torah —
but she is one who is not commanded and does it!
phrases.notes: Someone who is commanded gets more reward than someone who isn't, so her merit here is weaker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to 'merit of what?' and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that Torah study is the merit that delays her punishment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A woman is not commanded in Torah study, and voluntary performance earns less reward, so it could not be strong enough to delay punishment.

steps.title: Suggestion: the merit of a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Since Torah study was ruled out, the גמרא suggests the merit is from a מצוה that she performed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is the merit of a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new answer: the merit comes from מצוות she did, which she was commanded to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מצוות that a woman is obligated in give her full merit, so they avoid the problem with Torah study. This is still only a suggestion, and the next step challenges it.

keyTerms.meaning: The merit of doing a מצוה

phrases.english: Rather, it is the merit of a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected Torah-study answer with a new suggestion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The protecting merit may be from מצוות she performed, not from Torah study.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a מצוה protects only for a short time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 7 that a מצוה could delay punishment for years. It quotes רבי מנחם בר יוסי, who says a מצוה is like a lamp and protects only for a while.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can the merit of a מצוה really protect that much? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי מנחם בר יוסי explained the פסוק 'For a מצוה is a lamp and Torah is light.' The פסוק compares a מצוה to a lamp and Torah to light. A מצוה is compared to a lamp to teach you that a lamp gives protection only for a while, and so does a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave in step 7. If a מצוה protects only for a short time, how could it delay a סוטה's punishment for up to three years?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'נר מצוה' as a lamp, which lights only the spot where you hold it and only while it burns. So a מצוה protects only 'לפי שעה', for a limited time. That clashes with the idea that a מצוה could hold off punishment for years.

keyTerms.meaning: Merit: credit earned for a good deed that can protect a person
So much, to such a great extent
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? Opens a challenge from a teaching of the תנאים
A lamp: a small light you hold in your hand
For a limited time, only for the moment

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say a מצוה has no value. It says only that a מצוה's protection lasts a limited time, unlike Torah's.

phrases.aramaic: זְכוּת דְּמִצְוָה מִי מַגְּנָא כּוּלֵּי הַאי?
phrases.english: Does the merit of a מצוה protect that much?
But isn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי מְנַחֵם בַּר יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: This is how Rabbi Menachem bar Yosei explained:
"For a מצוה is a lamp and Torah is light,"
phrases.notes: משלי 6:23

phrases.english: the verse linked the מצוה to a lamp,
and the Torah to light.
The מצוה to a lamp, to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: מָה נֵר אֵינָהּ מְגִינָּה אֶלָּא לְפִי שָׁעָה —
phrases.english: just as a lamp protects only for a while,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִצְוָה אֵינָהּ מְגִינָּה אֶלָּא לְפִי שָׁעָה.
phrases.english: so too a מצוה protects only for a while.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְכוּת דְּמִצְוָה מִי מַגְּנָא כּוּלֵּי הַאי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7 that the delaying merit comes from a מצוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion in step 7 that a מצוה's merit delays the סוטה's punishment for up to three years.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא teaches that a מצוה, like a lamp, protects only for a limited time. So it cannot be the merit that holds off punishment for years.

steps.title: Torah is like sunlight and protects forever
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Torah is compared to light because it protects forever. A second פסוק shows that Torah protects in this world, at death, and in the world to come.
steps.simpleTranslation: Torah is compared to light to teach you that just as light protects forever, Torah protects forever. The פסוק also says: 'When you walk, it will guide you.' 'When you walk, it will guide you' means this world. 'When you lie down, it will watch over you' means death. 'And when you wake up, it will speak with you' means the time to come.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its comparison. Unlike a מצוה, Torah gives lasting protection, and it brings a פסוק to prove this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This half of the ברייתא sharpens the contrast with step 8: a lamp's protection is limited, but light protects 'לעולם', forever. The extra פסוק backs this up by showing that Torah's protection covers every stage of a person's existence: life, the grave, and after תחיית המתים.

keyTerms.meaning: Light, here the full light of day
And it says: brings an additional פסוק as support
The time to come, after תחיית המתים

steps.whyThisMatters: This contrast between a מצוה and Torah sets up the question the גמרא must answer next: what merit could protect a סוטה for years, if not Torah and not an ordinary מצוה?

phrases.english: And the Torah to light, to tell you:
just as light protects forever,
so too Torah protects forever.
And it says: "When you walk, it will guide you, etc."
phrases.notes: משלי 6:22

phrases.english: "When you walk, it will guide you" — this is this world.
"When you lie down, it will watch over you" — this is death.
"And when you wake up, it will speak with you" — in the time to come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from step 8 by explaining the Torah half of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That Torah gives permanent protection, unlike a מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 6:22, 'בהתהלכך תנחה אתך, בשכבך תשמור עליך, והקיצות היא תשיחך'

steps.title: Parable: a man walking alone in the dark
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins a parable about a man walking in deep darkness. He fears hidden obstacles, dangerous animals and bandits, and he does not know his way.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a man walking in the blackness of night and darkness. He is afraid of thorns, pits and thistles, and of wild animals and bandits, and he does not know which way he is going.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is setting up a parable to explain the difference between a מצוה and Torah. Here it only describes the man's dangers; the solutions come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parable lists three kinds of problems: obstacles on the ground (thorns, pits, thistles), dangers that roam at night (animals, bandits), and not knowing the way. Each kind will be solved by a different stage of light in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable, a story used to explain an idea
The blackness of night, the darkest part of the night

phrases.english: A parable: a man who was walking
in the blackness of night and darkness,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִתְיָירֵא מִן הַקּוֹצִים וּמִן הַפְּחָתִים וּמִן הַבַּרְקָנִים,
phrases.english: and he is afraid of the thorns, the pits and the thistles,
and of wild animals and bandits,
and he does not know which way he is walking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a parable to illustrate the lamp-versus-light contrast from steps 8 and 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man in total darkness faces three kinds of trouble: obstacles underfoot, roaming dangers, and not knowing the way.

steps.title: The torch, the dawn and the crossroads
steps.stepSummary: The parable continues. A torch saves the man from obstacles on the ground. Dawn also saves him from animals and bandits. Only when he reaches a crossroads is he saved from everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a torch comes his way, he is safe from the thorns, pits and thistles. But he is still afraid of wild animals and bandits, and he still does not know his way. Once dawn rises, he is safe from wild animals and bandits, but he still does not know his way. When he reaches a crossroads, he is saved from all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The parable shows stage by stage how each kind of light helps the man. The torch stands for a מצוה, and the dawn stands for Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The torch, like a מצוה, gives limited help: it lights only the ground nearby. Dawn, like Torah, is far stronger and also drives away the animals and bandits. Even so, full safety comes only at the crossroads, a final stage beyond both.
steps.whatToRemember: A מצוה is like a lamp or torch: real protection, but limited. Torah is like daylight: it protects forever. This is why the גמרא doubts that a מצוה alone could hold off the סוטה's punishment for years.

phrases.english: If a torch of fire comes his way —
phrases.notes: The torch stands for a מצוה, like the lamp in the פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: נִיצַּל מִן הַקּוֹצִים וּמִן הַפְּחָתִים וּמִן הַבַּרְקָנִים,
phrases.english: he is safe from the thorns, the pits and the thistles,

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲדַיִין מִתְיָירֵא מֵחַיָּה רָעָה וּמִן הַלִּיסְטִין,
phrases.english: but he is still afraid of wild animals and bandits,
and he does not know which way he is walking.
Once dawn rises —
phrases.notes: Dawn stands for Torah, the 'light' in the פסוק.

phrases.english: he is safe from wild animals and bandits,

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲדַיִין אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּאֵיזֶה דֶּרֶךְ מְהַלֵּךְ.
phrases.english: but he still does not know which way he is walking.
When he reaches a crossroads — he is saved from all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the parable begun in step 10 by showing how each stage of light solves another problem.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A torch (מצוה) gives limited protection, dawn (Torah) gives much greater protection, and the crossroads brings complete safety.

steps.title: A sin puts out a מצוה but not Torah
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a second reason why a מצוה is a lamp and תורה is light. A sin can put out the merit of a מצוה, but it cannot put out the merit of תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: a sin puts out the merit of a מצוה, but a sin does not put out the merit of Torah. As the verse says: 'Many waters cannot put out the love.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its comparison. It adds that sins can 'put out' a מצוה, like water putting out a lamp, but they cannot put out תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This strengthens the challenge from step 8. If sins put out a מצוה's merit, then the סוטה's sin should cancel her מצוה merit, so a מצוה cannot be what holds off her punishment. Only תורה survives sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Love; here a name for תורה

steps.whatToRemember: A מצוה is like a lamp that a sin can put out. תורה is like sunlight that no sin can put out.

phrases.english: Another explanation: a sin puts out a מצוה,
but a sin does not put out Torah,
as it says: 'Many waters cannot'
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 8:7. The 'many waters' are the sins.

phrases.english: 'put out the love.'
phrases.notes: The 'love' here is understood as the תורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that supports the challenge from step 8.
steps.raayaObject: A מצוה's merit is too weak to hold off the סוטה's punishment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the פסוק 'מים רבים לא יוכלו לכבות את האהבה'.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a מצוה still protects after it is done
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that a מצוה keeps protecting a person from suffering even after he has finished doing it. So a מצוה can hold off the סוטה's punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: A מצוה, while a person is busy doing it, protects him and saves him. When he is not busy with it, it protects him but does not save him. Torah, both while he is busy with it and when he is not, protects and saves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends the idea that the סוטה's merit comes from a מצוה. He splits the power of a מצוה into two parts: protecting and saving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Protects' means shielding from suffering and punishment. 'Saves' means rescuing from sin. A מצוה lowers its power after it is done, but it still protects, and that is enough to hold off the סוטה's punishment.
steps.confusionAlert: Two verbs are at work here: protecting and saving. Watch which one each item keeps when the person is not busy with it.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
A מצוה, at the time one is busy with it,
protects and saves;
phrases.notes: 'Protects' means from suffering. 'Saves' means from being pulled into sin.

phrases.english: at the time one is not busy with it,
protecting, it protects; saving, it does not save.
Torah, both at the time one is busy with it
and at the time one is not busy with it,
protects and saves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that a מצוה protects only briefly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the power of a מצוה into two parts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מצוה stops helping once it is done, so it cannot hold off punishment for years.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מצוה keeps protecting from suffering even after it is done, so it can hold off the סוטה's punishment.

steps.title: רבה: then why didn't Torah save דואג and אחיתופל?
steps.stepSummary: רבה attacks רב יוסף. If תורה always saves a person from sin, why did דואג and אחיתופל, who learned תורה, end up sinning?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה challenged this: But if so, didn't דואג and אחיתופל study Torah? Why didn't it protect them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה challenges רב יוסף's rule about תורה, using two great scholars who became famous sinners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said תורה saves from sin even when a person is not learning. Yet דואג and אחיתופל were scholars and still sinned badly. So רב יוסף's rule cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Two great scholars of דוד's time who sinned

phrases.english: Rabba challenged it:
But if so,

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹאֵג וַאֲחִיתוֹפֶל מִי לָא עָסְקִי בְּתוֹרָה?
phrases.english: Doeg and Achitofel, didn't they study Torah?
phrases.notes: See שמואל א chapters 21–22 and שמואל ב chapter 16.

phrases.english: Why didn't it protect them?
phrases.notes: He means protect them from sinning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's claim about תורה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that תורה saves from sin even when a person is not learning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דואג and אחיתופל learned תורה and still sinned, so תורה does not always save.

steps.title: רבא rearranges the rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new version. תורה saves from sin only while a person is learning, but it always protects from suffering. A מצוה always protects but never saves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Torah, while one is busy with it, protects and saves. When one is not busy with it, it protects but does not save. A מצוה, both while one is busy with it and when one is not, protects but does not save.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of רבה's challenge, רבא gives a corrected version of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now תורה saves from sin only during learning, which explains דואג and אחיתופל. A מצוה still protects from suffering even after it is done. So a מצוה can still hold off the סוטה's punishment.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: תורה protects always, but saves only while learning. A מצוה protects always, but never saves.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Torah, at the time one is busy with it,
protects and saves;
at the time one is not busy with it,
protecting, it protects; saving, it does not save.
A מצוה, both at the time one is busy with it
and at the time one is not busy with it,
protecting, it protects; saving, it does not save.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's version after רבה's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a corrected version of the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תורה saves from sin at all times.
steps.terutzMaskana: תורה saves only while one is learning. Both תורה and a מצוה protect from suffering at all times, so a מצוה can still hold off the סוטה's punishment.

steps.title: רבינא: it really is Torah merit, through her sons and husband
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the merit is תורה after all. A woman shares the reward of her sons' and husband's Torah learning, because she helps them learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really it is the merit of Torah. And as for what you said, that she is not commanded and does it anyway: granted, she is not commanded. But in reward for having their sons taught מקרא and משנה, and for waiting for their husbands until they come back from the בית מדרש, don't they share the reward with them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא takes a different approach. He goes back to the idea that was ruled out earlier: the merit comes from תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, Torah merit was ruled out because a woman is not commanded to learn. רבינא answers that her merit is not from her own learning. She shares in the learning of her sons and husband, because she makes it possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (going back to an earlier idea)

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא: a woman who helps her sons and husband learn תורה shares in their Torah merit. That merit can hold off the סוטה's punishment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the idea that people who support Torah learning share in its reward.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Really, it is the merit of Torah,
and as for what you said, 'she is not commanded and does it anyway,'
granted that she is not commanded,
in reward for having their sons taught Scripture and Mishna,
and waiting for their husbands
until they come back from the study hall,
don't they share with them?
phrases.notes: He means they share the reward of the men's Torah learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from רב יוסף and רבא, returning to Torah merit.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Returns to an idea that was ruled out and shows how it can work.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Torah merit can't apply to her, because a woman is not commanded to learn.
steps.terutzMaskana: She shares in the Torah merit of her sons and husband, and that merit holds off her punishment.

steps.title: What is the crossroads in the parable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the 'crossroads' in the parable stands for.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'the crossroads'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the 'crossroads' in the parable stands for. This question sets up three answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the parable, a man walking in the dark is fully safe only once he reaches the crossroads. The גמרא wants to know what that final, complete safety stands for in real life.

keyTerms.meaning: Crossroads, the point where the right road becomes clear

phrases.english: What is 'the crossroads'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבינא's answer, the גמרא goes back to explain a detail of the parable.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What real-life situation the 'crossroads' of the parable stands for.

steps.title: רב חסדא: A Torah scholar on his day of death
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the crossroads is a תלמיד חכם on the day he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This is a תלמיד חכם and the day of his death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the first answer. The crossroads is a תלמיד חכם on the day he dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At death, a תלמיד חכם who stayed with his learning sees clearly where he is going. That clarity is what it means to reach the crossroads and be safe from everything.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This is a Torah scholar and the day of death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The crossroads is a תלמיד חכם at the time of his death.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: A Torah scholar with fear of sin
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the crossroads is a תלמיד חכם who also has יראת חטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: This is a תלמיד חכם who has fear of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a second answer. The crossroads is a תלמיד חכם who also has יראת חטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to him, the full safety does not wait for death. It comes during life, when Torah knowledge and fear of sin are joined together.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
This is a Torah scholar and fear of sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same question, different from רב חסדא's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The crossroads is a תלמיד חכם who has fear of sin.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: A תלמיד חכם whose learning matches the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says the crossroads is a תלמיד חכם whose learning comes out according to the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: This is a תלמיד חכם whose learning comes out in line with the הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives a third answer. The crossroads is a תלמיד חכם whose conclusions match the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, the clear road is being right in learning. When a scholar keeps reaching the correct הלכה, that shows he is on the right path.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or discussion being learned

steps.whatToRemember: The crossroads has three explanations: a תלמיד חכם at his death (רב חסדא), a תלמיד חכם with fear of sin (רב נחמן בר יצחק), or a תלמיד חכם who reaches the correct הלכה (מר זוטרא).

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
This is a Torah scholar
whose learning comes out for him
in line with the halacha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The crossroads is a תלמיד חכם whose learning reaches the correct הלכה.

steps.title: Had דואג and אחיתופל understood this, they would not have chased דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again: a sin puts out a מצוה but not תורה. רב יוסף says that if דואג and אחיתופל had understood this, they would not have chased דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: a sin puts out a מצוה, but a sin does not put out תורה. רב יוסף said: רבי מנחם בר יוסי explained this פסוק as clearly as it was given at סיני. If דואג and אחיתופל had explained it this way, they would not have chased after דוד, as it says: 'saying, God has left him...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the ברייתא's line that a sin cannot put out תורה, so it can comment on it. רב יוסף says that not knowing this is what led דואג and אחיתופל to chase דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דואג and אחיתופל thought that דוד's sin had wiped out all his merit, so God had left him. They missed that his תורה still protected him. The פסוק 'God has left him' shows what they were thinking.

keyTerms.meaning: Puts out, like putting out a flame
Two great Torah scholars of דוד's time who turned against him
As it was given at סיני, meaning exactly right

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ברייתא. The גמרא is quoting the same ברייתא from step 12 again so that רב יוסף can comment on it.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
a sin puts out a מצוה,
but a sin does not put out Torah.
Rav Yosef said:
Rabbi Menachem bar Yosei explained
this verse as at Sinai,
phrases.notes: He means: just as clearly and correctly as when it was given at סיני.

phrases.english: and had Doeg and Achitofel explained it this way,
they would not have chased after David,
as it is written: 'Saying, God has left him, etc.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 71:11

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: דַּרְשֵׁיהּ רַבִּי מְנַחֵם בַּר יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the crossroads discussion and goes back to the ברייתא's second reason from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Knowing that a sin cannot put out תורה would have stopped דואג and אחיתופל from chasing דוד.

steps.title: The verse דואג and אחיתופל misread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which פסוק דואג and אחיתופל explained. They used 'He should not see in you anything indecent', but they did not know that a sin cannot put out תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they explain? 'He should not see in you anything indecent, and turn away from you.' But they did not know that a sin puts out a מצוה, and a sin does not put out תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which פסוק דואג and אחיתופל relied on, and answers right away. They read a פסוק that says God turns away from immorality, and they applied it to דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They reasoned that after דוד's sin, God had turned away from him. Their mistake was missing the rule that a sin cannot put out the merit of תורה. דוד's תורה still protected him.

keyTerms.meaning: Something indecent, here meaning forbidden relations

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the ברייתא's rule matters in real life. Misreading it led great scholars to turn against דוד המלך.

phrases.english: What did they explain?
'He should not see in you anything indecent, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים 23:15. The end of the פסוק says God will 'turn away from you.'

phrases.english: But they did not know
that a sin puts out a מצוה,
but a sin does not put out Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which פסוק רב יוסף was talking about in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They used דברים 23:15 to conclude that God had left דוד. They did not realize that his תורה could not be put out by his sin.

steps.title: What does 'he would be utterly scorned' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words 'בוז יבוזו לו' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'he would be utterly scorned'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the words 'בוז יבוזו לו' at the end of the ברייתא's פסוק. This sets up עולא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that if a man gave all his wealth for love, he would be scorned. Since תורה is compared to love, this could mean that money cannot buy a share in תורה. The גמרא now asks how to understand this.

phrases.english: What is 'he would be utterly scorned'?
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 8:7. This is the end of the same פסוק, 'many waters cannot put out the love', that the ברייתא used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from דואג and אחיתופל to the end of the פסוק the ברייתא quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the person the פסוק says would be scorned for giving his wealth?

steps.title: עולא: Not people like שמעון אחי עזריה or רבי יוחנן דבי נשיאה
steps.stepSummary: עולא begins his answer. The scorned person in the פסוק is not someone like שמעון אחי עזריה or רבי יוחנן דבי נשיאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Not like שמעון the brother of עזריה, and not like רבי יוחנן of the house of the נשיא...
steps.whatsHappening: עולא starts explaining whom the פסוק is not talking about. His sentence continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמעון learned תורה while his brother עזריה supported him. רבי יוחנן learned while the נשיא's household supported him. עולא is saying that supporting a scholar like this is not the scorned 'buying' the פסוק describes. This fits רבינא's idea that someone who helps others learn shares in their reward.

keyTerms.meaning: שמעון, the brother of עזריה, whose brother supported his learning
Of the house of the נשיא, the leader of the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: עולא's sentence is not finished here. Its ending, which says whom the פסוק does mean, comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Not like Shimon the brother of Azarya,
phrases.notes: His brother עזריה supported him so he could learn.

phrases.english: and not like Rabbi Yochanan of the house of the Nasi,
phrases.notes: He was supported by the נשיא's household while he learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: לָא כְּשִׁמְעוֹן אֲחִי עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is not speaking about cases where someone supports a scholar so he can learn. עולא finishes his answer in the next step.

steps.title: The Scorned One Is Like הלל and שבנא
steps.stepSummary: עולא completes his answer. The person scorned in the פסוק is someone like the case of הלל and שבנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like הלל and שבנא.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא finishes the answer he started in the last step. After saying who the פסוק is NOT talking about, he now says who it IS talking about. This short line sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24 עולא ruled out supporters like שמעון אחי עזריה and רבי יוחנן דבי נשיאה. The word אֶלָּא ('rather') turns to the positive side. The case of הלל and שבנא will be the example of someone the פסוק says is scorned.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather / but instead. It turns from what is wrong to what is right.
Hillel, the brother who learned Torah. This is not the famous הלל הזקן.
Shevna, הלל's brother, who went into business.

phrases.english: Rather, like Hillel and Shevna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes עולא's answer. Step 24 gave the negative side (not like these people), and this gives the positive side (but like these).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the person described as 'בוז יבוזו לו'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Someone like שבנא in the story of הלל and שבנא.

steps.title: רב דימי Tells the Story of the Two Brothers
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that הלל learned Torah and שבנא did business. In the end שבנא offered to combine their assets and split them.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came to Babylonia, he said: הלל and שבנא were brothers. הלל learned Torah and שבנא went into business. In the end שבנא said to הלל: Come, let us combine and divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב דימי's report to explain who הלל and שבנא were. שבנא, the rich brother, offers to pool everything and split it, so he would give money and get a share of הלל's Torah reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is לְסוֹף, 'in the end'. שבנא did not support הלל while he was learning. He tried to buy a share after the learning was already done. That is the difference from the supporters in step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came. This is used for a scholar who arrived in Babylonia from ארץ ישראל.
Did business / entered a business venture.
Let us combine and divide, meaning pool our assets and split them equally.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the supporters in step 24. They are not scorned. שבנא is the problem case because he wanted to buy a share 'in the end', after the learning was finished.

phrases.english: For when Rav Dimi came, he said:
Hillel and Shevna were brothers.
Hillel engaged in Torah,
Shevna went into business.
In the end, he said to him:
phrases.notes: Here 'he' is שבנא, speaking to his brother הלל.

phrases.english: Come, let us combine and divide!
phrases.notes: He means: I give you half my money, and you give me half the reward of your learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the story behind the name 'הלל and שבנא' that עולא just mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבנא, who did business, tried after the fact to trade half his wealth for half of הלל's Torah reward.

steps.title: The בת קול Rejects שבנא's Offer
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול answers with the פסוק 'אם יתן איש את כל הון ביתו', which ends 'בוז יבוזו לו'. Such an offer is scorned.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said: 'If a man would give all the wealth of his house' (for love, they would utterly scorn him).
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven itself answers שבנא's offer by quoting the very פסוק the גמרא asked about in step 23. This closes the explanation of 'בוז יבוזו לו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The part of the פסוק hidden in וְגוֹ׳ is 'באהבה בוז יבוזו לו'. Even all the money in a house cannot buy Torah that was already learned, and the attempt is scorned. This is how עולא's reading of the פסוק is shown.

keyTerms.meaning: The wealth of his house, meaning all his money.
'And so on'. The rest of the פסוק is left out but meant to be understood.

steps.whatToRemember: 'בוז יבוזו לו' is about someone like שבנא, who tries to buy a share of Torah after the learning is done. It is not about a supporter like שמעון אחי עזריה. Money cannot buy Torah after the fact.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a clear limit: supporting Torah learners is praised, but trying to buy a share of finished learning is rejected.

phrases.english: A Divine Voice came out and said:

phrases.aramaic: ״אִם יִתֵּן אִישׁ אֶת כׇּל הוֹן בֵּיתוֹ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "If a man would give all the wealth of his house, etc."
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 8:7. The part left out is 'באהבה בוז יבוזו לו', the exact words the גמרא asked about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives Heaven's answer to שבנא's offer and ties the story back to the פסוק from step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The scorn of 'בוז יבוזו לו' falls on someone who tries to buy a share in Torah learning after it was done, like שבנא.
